candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale manager Ian Watson believes his side showed their mettle in the 2-1 win at Fleetwood. Goals from Dajaune Brown and Aden Flint put Dale 2-0 up early on but they were forced into sterling rearguard action in the second half, especially after Tobi Adebayo-Rowling saw a second yellow card 21 minutes from time, with Mark Helm having reduced the deficit. Watson, who had come under fire during Dale’s slow start to the season, said: “That’s what we want to look like all the time. “I’m just really pleased we get to see what we’re actually working on, what we’re trying to look like, and how brave the boys were with the ball, how much courage they played with. “When they do that, it’s really hard for the opposition. I felt the first 20 was really pleasing, then I think we maybe played the scoreboard a little bit after that and self-preservation mode kicked in a little bit. “We got to half-time and I thought we regrouped, and started the second half really well. There’s so much I love about today’s performance, not just with the ball, but everything without the ball, and the heart and desire the boys showed as well. “I understand where the frustration comes from but my responsibility is to not listen to any noise, just focus and back myself as a coach, as a human as well. My mentality is strong and I believe in myself. But how amazing were the fans as well, they got us over the line.” Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor cut a frustrated figure having seen his side start slowly and then fail to break Dale down for an equaliser.

Drum kit sorted for bands, PA system sorted. Bratwurst sorted. Sorting hot drinks and sweet things. Local bands all sorted. Conkers collected. “The draft bar will sell beer made in Midd. Craft uses continental hops, best pint in Manchester. With Manchester stout on, and the Oktoberfest session lager. “Music, beer and food festival in a massive marquee in the middle of Middleton Gardens. This wonderful community effort shows how, together, we can make a real difference to people’s lives.” The Mayoress, Iram Faisal, speaking to Roch Valley Radio, said the event also gave people an opportunity to learn about the charities supported by the fund.

He was taken to hospital for treatment but, despite the best efforts of emergency services, he sadly died. Two men have been arrested in connection with the incident and remain in custody for questioning. Detectives from the Major Incident Team are now leading the investigation and are appealing for anyone who witnessed the incident, has information about what happened, or has relevant CCTV, mobile phone or dashcam footage to come forward. The victim’s family are being supported by specialist officers. Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan, from the Major Incident Team, said : “This is a heart-breaking incident in which a man has tragically lost his life. “Our thoughts are first and foremost with his family and loved ones who are being supported by specially trained officers at this incredibly difficult time.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale secured a 2-1 victory over Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium on September 26, 2026, despite playing the final 21 minutes with ten men following Tobi Adebayo-Rowling's dismissal.Dajaune Brown opened the scoring for the visiting side in the eighth minute with a right-footed finish from the center of the penalty area. Aden Flint doubled Rochdale's advantage six minutes later, striking into the bottom-left corner after Brown blocked an initial effort.Mark Helm brought Fleetwood Town back into the contest in the 30th minute. The midfielder received a pass from Aaron Loupalo-Bi outside the box and drove a right-footed shot into the bottom-right corner of the net.Fleetwood Town pushed for an equalizer before the break, but Rochdale goalkeeper Sam Waller maintained the visitors' lead by saving a header from captain Ched Evans and a tight-angle effort from Raff Cirino.Rochdale was reduced to ten players in the 69th minute when Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a foul on Loupalo-Bi. Fleetwood Town capitalized on the numerical advantage to create multiple opportunities in the closing stages.Waller made several key saves during the second half to deny Evans, Ronan Coughlan, and Lewis McCann. Fleetwood Town was unable to find a second goal despite five minutes of added time.Fleetwood Town manager Matt Lawlor adjusted his squad during the match, introducing Jake Batty for Kayden Hughes in the 64th minute and Coughlan for Adam Murphy in the 70th minute.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: There was an ‘incident’ on South Parade in Rochdale (Picture: Google Maps) Police have launched a murder investigation following an ‘incident’ in Rochdale, which led to the death of a man. Officers were called out to the town centre at around 1.30am today, where they found the 52-year-old unconscious after he was assaulted on South Parade, between The Old Bank bar and AST Hampsons Solicitors. Greater Manchester Police confirmed that Northwest Ambulance Service and GMP attended the scene. He was taken to hospital for treatment, where, despite the best efforts of emergency services, he died from his injuries. His family members are being supported by specialist officers. Two men are in custody and are being questioned in connection with the incident. The police are appealing for any witnesses or anyone with CCTV or mobile phone footage to come forward to assist with enquiries. Detective Chief Inspector Claire Brennan from the Major Incident Team said: ‘This is a heartbreaking incident in which a man has tragically lost his life. ‘Our thoughts are first and foremost with his family and loved ones who are being supported by specially trained officers at this incredibly difficult time.’ She added: ‘We understand an incident of this nature will also cause concern within the local community. ‘I want to reassure people that we have a dedicated team of detectives working to establish the full circumstances surrounding this incident and understand exactly what happened in the moments leading up to it.’ The investigation is ‘ongoing’, as an appeal has been launched directly to anyone who was in the South Parade area in the small hours on Saturday. Police are keen to hear from those who ‘may have witnessed the incident or seen anything suspicious before or afterwards’. ‘If you have any information, no matter how insignificant you think it may be, please come forward and speak to our officers on 101 or LiveChat, quoting log 250 of 26/09/2026. ‘Alternatively, contact independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.’ Get in touch with our news team by emailing us at webnews@metro.co.uk. The visitors raced into a two-goal lead inside 14 minutes, Dajaune Brown netting with a first-time finish from Glenn Middleton's cross in the eighth minute before Aden Flint doubled Dale's advantage, coolly slotting home after Brown's shot fell kindly into his path. Mark Helm hit back on the half-hour mark, pouncing on a loose ball in midfield and finishing neatly into the bottom corner. Fleetwood pushed hard for an equaliser, with Ched Evans' shot deflected inches wide, Raffaele Cirino hitting the side-netting and Aaron Loupalo-Bi narrowly wide with a fierce low drive. The home side dominated the second half but Lewis McCann clearing the bar by inches was as close as they got. Dale's task got even tougher on 69 minutes when Tobi Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a shirt pull. Goalkeeper Sam Waller then denied Evans and Flint got his head to Ronan Coughlan's goalbound shot as valiant defending, and Fleetwood's wayward finishing, saw Dale hold on for the win. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Libraries across the borough are teaming up with a local charity to help families make use of thousands of free pre-loved school uniforms and shoes. As families continue to manage the high costs of school uniform, there is growing demand for affordable alternatives, including a reliance on local charities like Uniform For All, which Rochdale Council is working with to support those who need extra help. Every day high-quality pre-loved items, including polo shirts, skirts, trousers, branded school blazers, coats and pumps, are given to families through the charity. Not every family has the resources to travel long distances to collect their orders and the borough’s library service is helping to collect these items so families can pick them up closer to where they live at their nearest library and save on additional travel costs. When residents come in to collect their orders, library staff are also on hand to provide them with additional cost-of-living information and related support, if they need it, alongside free wifi and computer access and other benefits linked to a free library membership. Cllr Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation, said: “We are proud to be supporting this valuable charity in distributing much-needed uniforms to our local families. “Sadly, we know demand is growing for these items so by utilising our libraries, we can help families access what they need within their communities.” Operating since 2020, Uniform For All currently provides more than 20,000 items to more than 3,000 families each year.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The season is underway and it has been a solid start. With Liverpool now up and running under new head coach Andoni Iraola , there is a little frustration the extended international break is threatening to check momentum after successive victories. With the transfer window now closed, the focus has been on the action with the Reds making early inroads in both the Champions League and Carabao Cup ahead of what will be a busy period on their return to action in just over a fortnight. We have been asking for your questions on the current state of play at Anfield , and here we take a punt at providing some answers... Pete asks: Ian, in all your experience, is that the first time you’ve known a match to be interrupted by fireworks? In my 66 years watching elite level football, it’s the first one I can remember. Enjoyed your match report! Thanks, Pete. The game the gentleman is referring to was the Jersey Mike's Trophy - no, I don't either - clash Liverpool under-21s played at Rochdale on Tuesday evening . Having been reduced to 10 men in the first half, the young Reds were level at 1-1 when fireworks started to be let off by somebody outside one of the stands behind a goal. This continued for a few minutes until a few of the pyrotechnics landed near the pitch, at which point the referee's assistant handed one over to the main official, who stopped the game for a few minutes while the miscreants were dealt with. I've never known that happen before. But there was some comparison during the Covid era when, during Liverpool's comedy 7-2 loss at an empty Villa Park in October 2020, some Aston Villa fans turned up outside the stadium at half-time and started letting off fireworks at the start of the second half to celebrate their team running away with the win. None landed inside, though. In the game itself on Tuesday, Liverpool went 3-1 down but scored twice in the time added on due to the fireworks delay and then won 7-6 on penalties. Quite the night, let me tell you. And that's before even considering the immense takeaway that was consumed before the not-that-long-really journey home. Peter77 asks: How close did Anthony Gordon come to signing for us? See this week he's been talking about how he was a Red growing up. That Anthony Gordon grew up a Liverpool fan has been common knowledge for a long time. And so too is the fact he was extremely close to moving to Anfield in 2024 - and could also have made the transfer this summer. Two years ago, Newcastle United offered Gordon to the Reds in exchange for £30million and Joe Gomez , only to then pull the plug on the deal. candidates.source_body_excerpt: RivingtonHark, on behalf of Rochdale Borough Council, has secured British clothing retailer Peacocks on a long-term lease for a 10,181 sq ft unit at Rochdale Riverside, taking the scheme to 92% occupancy. The run of new lettings follows a 15.3% year-on-year footfall increase at Rochdale Riverside, with almost 200,000 visiting during July, continuing an upward year-on-year trend throughout 2026. The 200,000sq ft open-air scheme is anchored by a 50,000sq ft M&S store and a six-screen Real Cinema, and is home to leading national retailers including Next, H&M, Boots, and JD Sports. Ollie Holland, asset manager for Rochdale Riverside at RivingtonHark, said: “The letting brings another nationally recognised retailer to Rochdale Riverside, activating a prominent, centrally located unit and further strengthening the diverse and growing fashion offer. The addition of Peacocks reflects robust demand for well situated space and continued confidence from national and regional occupiers in the long-term appeal of Rochdale Riverside. “Rochdale Riverside is another example of how we work closely with local authorities like Rochdale Borough Council to deliver long-term value across town and city centre schemes. With footfall continuing to grow and further lettings in the pipeline we look forward to building on this continued momentum.” Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for regeneration and housing at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “It’s great to see Rochdale Riverside going from strength to strength with another new store signing up. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Pioneering digital autopsies could cut the need for invasive post-mortems by up to 80 per cent, reducing the distress caused to grieving loved ones. The innovative service is being delivered by the Coroner’s Office for Greater Manchester, in partnership with the NHS, specialist post-mortem imaging provider Anubix, and medical imaging provider TIC Health. Working with pathologists, radiologists and mortuary staff at the Northern Care Alliance the coroner’s office will, where appropriate, provide computed tomography (CT) scanning to help inform a person’s cause of death. Teams will use post-mortem imaging to check if a cause of death can be determined without the need for traditional invasive post-mortems, a process that can cause further distress to relatives during the grieving process across Rochdale, Bury, and Oldham. A number of scans a week will be carried out using the new technology, with a long-term ambition of speeding up the service provided for relatives following the loss of a loved one. Cllr Neil Emmott, leader of Rochdale Council, said: “This is a highly sensitive issue that has been carefully handled. “Working in partnership across the health sector, this will help to futureproof the coroner’s service and ensure families and loved ones continue to get the best possible support. “I know from speaking with residents across Heywood, Middleton, Pennines and Rochdale how invasive post-mortems often causes additional anxiety at a time of grief, so this is a timely and welcome new service.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The Liverpool FC U21s progressed through the hilariously named EFL Jersey Mike’s Trophy on Tuesday night. Away at League Two side Rochdale, and a man down after Mor Talla Ndiaye got himself sent off midway through the first half at the 21 minute mark, Liverpool went down 1-0 after Devante Rodney opened the scoring for the hosts from outside the box. Liverpool’s Will Wright then equalised wtih a sensational solo run: [Media: https://twitter.com/JerseyMikesTpy/status/2102507425974587438?s=20] A pair of Ian Henderson goals for the hosts, including a sublime lob of Liverpool keeper Harvey Davies from outside the box had the hosts looking like they’d progress, only for a pair of inury-time goals from substitutes Ben Trueman and Josh Sonni-Lambie to tie up the game. Sonni-Lambe scored virtually with the last kick of the game to send Robe Page’s side into a penalty shootout, which they won 7-6. What a result for the young lads.

I’m only sorry these two characters couldn’t wait a few more weeks before invading my privacy, as I’ve just started going back to the gym, and I might have looked even more fabulous than I already did at the Manchester Pride 2026 event most of the photos are from. “Joking aside, there are more revealing photos of many straight men and women at the beach or at the gym all over social media, I am not remotely ashamed to have a social and dating life, and it obviously affects not a jot my work as a proud ward councillor for the brilliant people of North Heywood. candidates.source_body_excerpt: The kick pitch is located by The Burnside Centre in Middleton. Residents in Middleton are campaigning for a replacement football pitch after plans were announced to turn the existing site into a car park. Campaigners say the pitch in Burnside Crescent on the Langley Estate is a community hub as well as somewhere people can play football and other sports. The pitch, which is next to the Burnside Centre, is one of three on the estate, and the car park will be for the centre. Families say they have been told replacement facilities will be provided at Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Council's planned Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. But they are campaigning for the new pitch to be created on land next to the original. The Burnside Centre said it understands why people are disappointed to see the pitch decommissioned, but said one of the reasons the decision was made related to concerns about antisocial behaviour. It added: "The pitch, which dates back to the late 1990s, had reached the end of its expected lifespan and required significant investment to remain operational." Resident Kelly Burton has four children, three of whom use the football pitch regularly.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Jamie Dale said rehabilitated ex-offenders need to be part of the support process for prison leavers A former prisoner who runs a support network for ex-offenders said government plans to release inmates early would fail to ease prison overcrowding without support from people who had experienced the system themselves. Jamie Dale, 47, from Rochdale, in Greater Manchester, spent more than 11 years in prison for his involvement in organised crime. He now runs the Old Lags Network, which aims to cut reoffending and bridge the gap between prison and the community. He said many prisoners "fall through the cracks" after release. "Most of the people who return quite quickly have not got great family networks," he said. Dale set up the Old Lags Network in September 2025 to provide support to prison leavers Dale said involving ex-offenders in developing solutions would "drastically reduce the amount of people being recalled to prison". "A lot of them can just end up sleeping on the streets," he said.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Liverpool U21s head coach Rob Page lauded the character of his side after producing a remarkable comeback to draw 3-3 at Rochdale in the Jersey Mike's Trophy. Despite playing 70 minutes with 10 men and trailing 3-1 entering second-half stoppage time, the young Reds avoided defeat in their northern Group H opener on Tuesday night. Substitutes Ben Trueman and Josh Sonni-Lambie netted in minutes 94 and 96 respectively to level the affair and take it to a penalty shootout, which Page's side won 7-6 to claim a bonus point. Speaking to reporters afterwards, Page said: "I mean, what character and resilience the boys showed to come back not only from the sending-off early on in the game, but to show character to see the game through. "I thought the substitutes came on and made a difference, gave us the fresh legs in the middle of the park that we needed. So, nothing but praise for that." He added: "We talk about being proud to wear the jersey. And when you wear the badge, there comes a level of expectation when you go out and play for Liverpool. "So, they know that myself and Jay [Spearing], who's played for the club, won't accept anything less than 100 per cent. So, they've got that built-in resilience. It's the character that we want in the team. "We've tried to change the mentality certainly in the 12 months that I've been here and I'm seeing it every day in training. The intensity of training has increased and they've got that winning mentality.
